paragraphs.title: Joseph Reveals Himself to His Brothers

easy.question: Who could not restrain himself?
answers: Joseph
His brothers
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Joseph could not restrain himself and asked to be left alone with his brothers.

easy.question: What did the Egyptians and Pharaoh’s household hear?
answers: The brothers’ words
Joseph’s weeping
Pharaoh’s voice
easy.explanation: Joseph wept aloud, and the Egyptians and Pharaoh’s household heard him.

easy.question: How did the brothers react when Joseph told them who he was?
answers: They rejoiced immediately
They fled from Egypt
They were troubled and could not answer
easy.explanation: The brothers were troubled by Joseph’s presence and could not answer him.

medium.question: What did Joseph do immediately after asking everyone to leave him?
answers: He left Pharaoh’s palace
He began to weep aloud
He asked about his father
medium.explanation: After everyone left, Joseph wept aloud; only afterward did he speak to his brothers.

medium.question: What does the phrase “could not restrain himself” mean in this passage?
answers: He could no longer hide his feelings
He moved away from his brothers
He prepared to leave
medium.explanation: Joseph could no longer hide his emotions, so he wept and revealed himself to his brothers.

medium.question: Why could the brothers not answer Joseph?
answers: They were troubled by the meeting and his position
They could not hear his voice
Joseph ordered them to be silent
medium.explanation: The verse says that they were troubled at his presence, so they could not answer him.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Joseph’s asking everyone to leave before revealing his identity?
answers: He wanted the meeting with his brothers to be private
He did not want to speak with his brothers
He was afraid of Pharaoh’s household
challenge.explanation: Joseph made sure no one else was present, suggesting that he wanted to reveal himself to his brothers privately.

challenge.question: Why were the brothers especially troubled when Joseph said, “I am Joseph”?
answers: They thought Joseph was dead
They realized that the ruler before them was the brother they had sold
Joseph ordered them to leave Egypt
challenge.explanation: They discovered that Joseph, whom they had sold, was alive and standing before them in a powerful position in Egypt.

challenge.question: What does Joseph emphasize by saying, “I am Joseph,” and adding, “your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt”?
answers: That he did not know his brothers
That he wanted to hide his past
Both his family relationship and the sale
challenge.explanation: Joseph emphasizes that he is both their brother and the person they sold into Egypt, connecting his present identity with their past deed.

questions.question: What can we infer from Joseph’s asking everyone to leave before revealing his identity?
answers: He wanted the meeting with his brothers to be private
He did not want to speak with his brothers
He was afraid of Pharaoh’s household
questions.explanation: Joseph made sure no one else was present, suggesting that he wanted to reveal himself to his brothers privately.

questions.question: Why were the brothers especially troubled when Joseph said, “I am Joseph”?
answers: They thought Joseph was dead
They realized that the ruler before them was the brother they had sold
Joseph ordered them to leave Egypt
questions.explanation: They discovered that Joseph, whom they had sold, was alive and standing before them in a powerful position in Egypt.

questions.question: What does Joseph emphasize by saying, “I am Joseph,” and adding, “your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt”?
answers: That he did not know his brothers
That he wanted to hide his past
Both his family relationship and the sale
questions.explanation: Joseph emphasizes that he is both their brother and the person they sold into Egypt, connecting his present identity with their past deed.

paragraphs.title: God’s Providence and Joseph’s Mission to Save Lives

easy.question: Why does Joseph tell his brothers not to be grieved or angry?
answers: Because he had forgotten what they did
Because God sent him to preserve life
Because the famine had ended
easy.explanation: Joseph explains that God sent him to Egypt so that lives could be preserved during the famine.

easy.question: How long had the famine lasted, and how many more years would it continue?
answers: One year, plus two more
Three years, plus four more
Two years, plus five more
easy.explanation: Joseph says that two years of famine had passed, and five more years would come without plowing or harvest.

easy.question: How does Joseph describe his positions in Egypt?
answers: A father to Pharaoh, lord of his house, and ruler throughout Egypt
Captain of the army and king of Egypt
A farmer, merchant, and servant
easy.explanation: Joseph says that God made him a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler throughout Egypt.

medium.question: What connection does Joseph make between being sold into Egypt and saving his family?
answers: God sent him ahead of his family to preserve their lives
His brothers sold him so that he could become a ruler
The sale caused the famine to end immediately
medium.explanation: Joseph does not ignore the sale, but explains that God used it to bring him to Egypt ahead of the family and save them during the famine.

medium.question: What does “earing” mean in the phrase “there shall neither be earing nor harvest”?
answers: Rain
Plowing or cultivating the land
Joy
medium.explanation: In the phrase “neither be earing nor harvest,” “earing” refers to plowing or working the land.

medium.question: What was one purpose of God’s sending Joseph to Egypt?
answers: To punish his brothers
To bring the family back to Canaan
To preserve a remnant of the family and save their lives
medium.explanation: Joseph says that God sent him to preserve a remnant in the earth and save their lives by a great deliverance.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Joseph’s movement from “ye sold me” to “God did send me”?
answers: Joseph acknowledges his brothers’ deed but also sees God’s plan of salvation
Joseph claims that his brothers had no part in selling him
Joseph thinks the sale had no effect on his life
challenge.explanation: Joseph mentions that his brothers sold him, but emphasizes that God used the result to preserve lives.

challenge.question: What total length of the famine can be inferred from these verses?
answers: Two years
Seven years
Ten years
challenge.explanation: Two years had already passed, and five more years would remain without plowing or harvest, making seven years in all.

challenge.question: How should we understand the phrase “he hath made me a father to Pharaoh”?
answers: Joseph was Pharaoh’s biological father
Joseph became a teacher only to Pharaoh’s children
Joseph received the position of a senior adviser with authority before Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: In the context of Joseph’s other positions, “a father to Pharaoh” describes a powerful adviser and authority figure, not literal fatherhood.

questions.question: What can we infer from Joseph’s movement from “ye sold me” to “God did send me”?
answers: Joseph acknowledges his brothers’ deed but also sees God’s plan of salvation
Joseph claims that his brothers had no part in selling him
Joseph thinks the sale had no effect on his life
questions.explanation: Joseph mentions that his brothers sold him, but emphasizes that God used the result to preserve lives.

questions.question: What total length of the famine can be inferred from these verses?
answers: Two years
Seven years
Ten years
questions.explanation: Two years had already passed, and five more years would remain without plowing or harvest, making seven years in all.

questions.question: How should we understand the phrase “he hath made me a father to Pharaoh”?
answers: Joseph was Pharaoh’s biological father
Joseph became a teacher only to Pharaoh’s children
Joseph received the position of a senior adviser with authority before Pharaoh
questions.explanation: In the context of Joseph’s other positions, “a father to Pharaoh” describes a powerful adviser and authority figure, not literal fatherhood.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Invites Jacob and the Family to Egypt

easy.question: Who said that God had made him lord over all Egypt?
answers: Joseph
Jacob
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Joseph told his brothers to say to their father, “God hath made me lord of all Egypt.”

easy.question: In what land did Joseph ask Jacob and his family to live?
answers: Canaan
Goshen
Midian
easy.explanation: Joseph told Jacob, “Thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen.”

easy.question: Whom did Joseph ask them to bring down to Egypt?
answers: Pharaoh
Only his brothers
His father
easy.explanation: At the end of the passage, Joseph asks them to bring his father to him.

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask his family to come to Egypt?
answers: Because five more years of famine remained
Because he wanted to leave Egypt
Because Pharaoh ordered them to leave
medium.explanation: Joseph wanted to provide for his family during the remaining years of famine so that they would not become poor.

medium.question: What does “I will nourish thee” mean in this passage?
answers: I will punish you
I will feed and care for you
I will send you back
medium.explanation: Because the family was facing famine, Joseph promised to provide them with food and what they needed.

medium.question: What order of actions did Joseph request from his brothers?
answers: Stay in Egypt and then tell Jacob
Build a house in Goshen and return to Canaan
Tell Jacob about Joseph and then bring him to Egypt
medium.explanation: First they were to tell Jacob that Joseph was alive and powerful in Egypt, and then quickly bring him down.

challenge.question: Why does Joseph emphasize, “your eyes see” and “it is my mouth that speaketh unto you”?
answers: To prove that he himself was Joseph
To tell them to look at all of Egypt
To ask them to close their eyes
challenge.explanation: Joseph emphasizes that they can see him and hear his voice so they will know that he is truly their brother Joseph.

challenge.question: What can we learn from Joseph’s mentioning the flocks, herds, and “all that thou hast”?
answers: Only the property would come to Egypt
The invitation included the whole family and their possessions
The family had to sell all its possessions
challenge.explanation: Joseph invited not only Jacob and his sons, but also their animals and possessions, so they could move together to Egypt.

challenge.question: What do the words “haste” and “tarry not” add to Joseph’s request?
answers: The journey to Egypt was unimportant
Joseph wanted them to wait until the famine ended
They needed to act urgently and not delay
challenge.explanation: These words emphasize urgency: the brothers were to return to Jacob quickly and bring him to Egypt without delay.

questions.question: Why does Joseph emphasize, “your eyes see” and “it is my mouth that speaketh unto you”?
answers: To prove that he himself was Joseph
To tell them to look at all of Egypt
To ask them to close their eyes
questions.explanation: Joseph emphasizes that they can see him and hear his voice so they will know that he is truly their brother Joseph.

questions.question: What can we learn from Joseph’s mentioning the flocks, herds, and “all that thou hast”?
answers: Only the property would come to Egypt
The invitation included the whole family and their possessions
The family had to sell all its possessions
questions.explanation: Joseph invited not only Jacob and his sons, but also their animals and possessions, so they could move together to Egypt.

questions.question: What do the words “haste” and “tarry not” add to Joseph’s request?
answers: The journey to Egypt was unimportant
Joseph wanted them to wait until the famine ended
They needed to act urgently and not delay
questions.explanation: These words emphasize urgency: the brothers were to return to Jacob quickly and bring him to Egypt without delay.

paragraphs.title: Reconciliation and Weeping Among the Brothers

easy.question: Whose neck did Joseph fall upon and weep?
answers: Benjamin’s
Reuben’s
Judah’s
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph fell upon Benjamin’s neck and wept.

easy.question: What did Benjamin do while Joseph wept?
answers: He spoke with his brothers
He wept upon Joseph’s neck
He left the room
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Benjamin wept upon his neck.”

easy.question: What did Joseph do to all his brothers?
answers: He gave them gifts
He asked them questions
He kissed them and wept upon them
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph kissed all his brothers and wept upon them.

medium.question: What happened in the order described by the verses?
answers: Joseph fell on Benjamin’s neck, kissed his brothers, and then they talked with him
The brothers spoke with Joseph, and then he kissed them
Benjamin spoke with Joseph, and then Joseph left
medium.explanation: First Joseph wept with Benjamin, then kissed and wept with all his brothers, and afterward they spoke with him.

medium.question: What does “he kissed” mean in the phrase “he kissed all his brethren”?
answers: He called them
He kissed them
He became angry with them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Joseph showing affection to his brothers after weeping with them.

medium.question: What was the result of the weeping and meeting between Joseph and his brothers?
answers: The brothers talked with Joseph
The brothers immediately returned to Canaan
Joseph hid himself from them
medium.explanation: The verse says that afterward his brothers talked with him; the conversation followed the emotional meeting.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Joseph and Benjamin both weeping on each other’s neck?
answers: Their meeting was deeply emotional and expressed a close family bond
They did not know each other
They were arguing about something
challenge.explanation: Their mutual weeping during the embrace expresses the intensity of their feelings and their brotherly bond.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “after that” emphasize?
answers: The brothers spoke before Joseph met them
The brothers spoke only after the weeping and kisses
The brothers did not want to speak with Joseph
challenge.explanation: The phrase establishes the order clearly: the emotional reunion came first, and the conversation followed.

challenge.question: What is the difference between the description of the meeting with Benjamin and the meeting with the other brothers?
answers: Joseph spoke with Benjamin but not with the others
Joseph was angry with Benjamin but loved the others
Benjamin received a special embrace and weeping, followed by Joseph’s kissing and weeping with all his brothers
challenge.explanation: The verses begin with a special personal moment between Joseph and Benjamin, and then describe Joseph’s emotional response to all his brothers.

questions.question: What can we understand from Joseph and Benjamin both weeping on each other’s neck?
answers: Their meeting was deeply emotional and expressed a close family bond
They did not know each other
They were arguing about something
questions.explanation: Their mutual weeping during the embrace expresses the intensity of their feelings and their brotherly bond.

questions.question: What does the phrase “after that” emphasize?
answers: The brothers spoke before Joseph met them
The brothers spoke only after the weeping and kisses
The brothers did not want to speak with Joseph
questions.explanation: The phrase establishes the order clearly: the emotional reunion came first, and the conversation followed.

questions.question: What is the difference between the description of the meeting with Benjamin and the meeting with the other brothers?
answers: Joseph spoke with Benjamin but not with the others
Joseph was angry with Benjamin but loved the others
Benjamin received a special embrace and weeping, followed by Joseph’s kissing and weeping with all his brothers
questions.explanation: The verses begin with a special personal moment between Joseph and Benjamin, and then describe Joseph’s emotional response to all his brothers.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh Invites the Family to Egypt

easy.question: Who heard that Joseph’s brothers had arrived in Egypt?
answers: Pharaoh and his household
Jacob and his sons
The king of Canaan
easy.explanation: The report was heard in Pharaoh’s house, where they learned that Joseph’s brothers had come.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh tell Joseph’s brothers to do with their animals?
answers: Sell them
Load them and go to Canaan
Leave them in Egypt
easy.explanation: Pharaoh told them to load their beasts and go to the land of Canaan.

easy.question: Whom did Pharaoh command them to bring to Egypt?
answers: Only Joseph
Only their neighbors
Their father and their households
easy.explanation: Pharaoh told the brothers to bring their father and their households to him in Egypt.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh tell them to take wagons from Egypt?
answers: To carry the children and wives and bring their father
To sell them in Canaan
To bring new animals to Pharaoh
medium.explanation: The wagons were for the children and wives, and for bringing their father Jacob.

medium.question: What does “eat the fat of the land” mean in this passage?
answers: Eat the fat of the animals
Enjoy the finest produce and abundance of the land
Eat only what was left in the land
medium.explanation: Here “fat” means the best and richest portion; Pharaoh was promising them the good of Egypt.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: The brothers arrive in Canaan, and then Pharaoh hears about them
Jacob arrives in Egypt, and then the brothers receive wagons
Pharaoh hears about the brothers, commands that the family be brought, and promises them Egypt’s good
medium.explanation: First the report reaches Pharaoh’s house, then Pharaoh gives instructions, and finally he promises the family the best of Egypt.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command, “regard not your stuff”?
answers: They should leave their belongings because Egypt would provide what they needed
They were forbidden to bring their family
They had to sell all their possessions before leaving
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh told them not to worry about the belongings they left behind because the good of Egypt would be theirs.

challenge.question: What can we learn from Pharaoh’s giving Joseph’s brothers instructions himself?
answers: Joseph was not allowed to speak with them
Pharaoh supported bringing Joseph’s family and gave it his authority
Pharaoh did not know who the brothers were
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh not only agreed to their coming, but instructed them how to proceed and promised them Egypt’s abundance.

challenge.question: What direction was the family traveling according to these verses?
answers: From Egypt to Canaan
From Canaan to another land
From Canaan to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The brothers were to return to Canaan, bring their father and households, and then come to Egypt.

questions.question: What can we infer from the command, “regard not your stuff”?
answers: They should leave their belongings because Egypt would provide what they needed
They were forbidden to bring their family
They had to sell all their possessions before leaving
questions.explanation: Pharaoh told them not to worry about the belongings they left behind because the good of Egypt would be theirs.

questions.question: What can we learn from Pharaoh’s giving Joseph’s brothers instructions himself?
answers: Joseph was not allowed to speak with them
Pharaoh supported bringing Joseph’s family and gave it his authority
Pharaoh did not know who the brothers were
questions.explanation: Pharaoh not only agreed to their coming, but instructed them how to proceed and promised them Egypt’s abundance.

questions.question: What direction was the family traveling according to these verses?
answers: From Egypt to Canaan
From Canaan to another land
From Canaan to Egypt
questions.explanation: The brothers were to return to Canaan, bring their father and households, and then come to Egypt.

paragraphs.title: Preparations for the Journey and Gifts

easy.question: What did Joseph give his brothers for the journey?
answers: Provision
Houses
Books
easy.explanation: Joseph gave them provision for the way.

easy.question: How much silver did Joseph give Benjamin?
answers: One hundred pieces
Three hundred pieces
Five hundred pieces
easy.explanation: Joseph gave Benjamin three hundred pieces of silver.

easy.question: To whom did Joseph give five changes of raiment?
answers: Reuben
Jacob
Benjamin
easy.explanation: Benjamin received five changes of raiment, while each of the other brothers received one.

medium.question: Why did Joseph give his brothers wagons and provisions?
answers: To help them on their journey
So they could fight in Egypt
So they would remain in Egypt
medium.explanation: The wagons and provisions were meant to help the brothers and Jacob’s family travel to Egypt.

medium.question: What does “provision” mean in the phrase “gave them provision for the way”?
answers: Festive clothing
Food and supplies for the journey
Gifts for Pharaoh
medium.explanation: The words “for the way” show that provision means food and supplies needed during the journey.

medium.question: What did Joseph do after giving gifts and provisions to his brothers and father?
answers: He traveled with them
He returned to Jacob’s house
He sent his brothers away and warned them not to quarrel on the way
medium.explanation: Joseph sent his brothers away and told them, “See that ye fall not out by the way.”

challenge.question: What detail shows that Benjamin received special treatment from Joseph?
answers: He received three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of raiment
He received only one wagon
He received provisions like his father
challenge.explanation: Each brother received one change of clothing, but Benjamin received five changes and three hundred pieces of silver.

challenge.question: What did the ten she-asses sent to Jacob carry?
answers: Silver and clothing
Corn, bread, and food for the journey
Wagons and horses
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes the asses carrying Egypt’s good from the she-asses carrying corn, bread, and food for the journey.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Joseph’s warning, “See that ye fall not out by the way”?
answers: The journey was very short
The brothers were forbidden to speak to one another
Joseph feared that they would become angry or quarrel on the journey
challenge.explanation: The warning suggests that Joseph was concerned they might argue or become angry with one another during the trip.

questions.question: What detail shows that Benjamin received special treatment from Joseph?
answers: He received three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of raiment
He received only one wagon
He received provisions like his father
questions.explanation: Each brother received one change of clothing, but Benjamin received five changes and three hundred pieces of silver.

questions.question: What did the ten she-asses sent to Jacob carry?
answers: Silver and clothing
Corn, bread, and food for the journey
Wagons and horses
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes the asses carrying Egypt’s good from the she-asses carrying corn, bread, and food for the journey.

questions.question: What can we understand from Joseph’s warning, “See that ye fall not out by the way”?
answers: The journey was very short
The brothers were forbidden to speak to one another
Joseph feared that they would become angry or quarrel on the journey
questions.explanation: The warning suggests that Joseph was concerned they might argue or become angry with one another during the trip.

paragraphs.title: The News Is Told to Jacob

easy.question: Where did the brothers arrive after leaving Egypt?
answers: The land of Canaan
The land of the Philistines
The land of Edom
easy.explanation: The brothers went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.

easy.question: What did the brothers tell Jacob about Joseph?
answers: That Joseph had left Egypt
That Joseph was alive and ruled Egypt
That Joseph had moved to Canaan
easy.explanation: They told Jacob that Joseph was still alive and was governor over all Egypt.

easy.question: What did Jacob see that caused his spirit to revive?
answers: The land of Egypt
Joseph himself
The wagons Joseph had sent
easy.explanation: Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, and his spirit revived.

medium.question: Why did Jacob initially not believe his sons?
answers: He did not recognize them
The news that Joseph was alive was hard to believe
They were still in Egypt
medium.explanation: Jacob did not immediately believe the report that Joseph was alive and ruling in Egypt.

medium.question: What did the brothers do after Jacob heard the news about Joseph?
answers: They immediately returned to Egypt
They left the land
They told him Joseph’s words and showed him the wagons
medium.explanation: The brothers supported their report by telling Jacob everything Joseph had said and showing him the wagons.

medium.question: What does “Jacob’s heart fainted” mean in this passage?
answers: His heart weakened and he lost his strength
His heart was filled with joy
His heart became angry with his sons
medium.explanation: In context, the phrase means that Jacob was overwhelmed and weakened by the shocking news.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Jacob’s being convinced after seeing the wagons?
answers: The wagons were a gift for Pharaoh
The brothers had told him nothing
He received tangible proof that Joseph had sent them
challenge.explanation: The wagons were visible evidence that Joseph was alive and had sent them to bring his father.

challenge.question: What change in Jacob’s emotions is described in the passage?
answers: From disbelief to renewed spirit and joy
From joy to anger
From fear to indifference
challenge.explanation: At first Jacob did not believe his sons, but after hearing Joseph’s words and seeing the wagons, his spirit revived.

challenge.question: What is the correct sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Jacob saw the wagons, and then the brothers arrived from Egypt
The brothers arrived from Egypt, told Jacob that Joseph was alive, and then showed him the wagons
Joseph came to Canaan, and then the brothers said he was alive
challenge.explanation: First the brothers came from Egypt to Canaan, then they told Jacob that Joseph was alive, and finally they showed him the wagons.

questions.question: What can we infer from Jacob’s being convinced after seeing the wagons?
answers: The wagons were a gift for Pharaoh
The brothers had told him nothing
He received tangible proof that Joseph had sent them
questions.explanation: The wagons were visible evidence that Joseph was alive and had sent them to bring his father.

questions.question: What change in Jacob’s emotions is described in the passage?
answers: From disbelief to renewed spirit and joy
From joy to anger
From fear to indifference
questions.explanation: At first Jacob did not believe his sons, but after hearing Joseph’s words and seeing the wagons, his spirit revived.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Jacob saw the wagons, and then the brothers arrived from Egypt
The brothers arrived from Egypt, told Jacob that Joseph was alive, and then showed him the wagons
Joseph came to Canaan, and then the brothers said he was alive
questions.explanation: First the brothers came from Egypt to Canaan, then they told Jacob that Joseph was alive, and finally they showed him the wagons.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Sets Out to See Joseph

easy.question: Who was alive according to Israel’s words?
answers: Joseph
Reuben
Benjamin
easy.explanation: Israel said, “Joseph my son is yet alive,” meaning that Joseph was still alive.

easy.question: What did Israel want to do?
answers: Stay at home
Go and see Joseph
Search for his brothers
easy.explanation: Israel said, “I will go and see him,” expressing his desire to see Joseph.

easy.question: When did Israel want to see Joseph?
answers: Before it rained
Before Joseph arrived
Before he died
easy.explanation: Israel wanted to see Joseph “before I die.”

medium.question: What caused Israel to want to go and see Joseph?
answers: The news that Joseph was alive
The desire to find a new land
His brothers’ command
medium.explanation: When Israel understood that his son Joseph was alive, he wanted to go and see him.

medium.question: What does “before” mean in the phrase “I will go and see him before I die”?
answers: After
Earlier than
Instead of
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Israel wanted to see Joseph before his own death.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Israel sees Joseph, then hears that he is alive
Israel dies, then decides to go
Israel hears that Joseph is alive, then wants to go and see him
medium.explanation: First Israel says that Joseph is alive, and then he expresses his desire to go and see him.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Israel’s saying, “It is enough”?
answers: The news that Joseph was alive brought Israel great joy
Israel wanted to wait several more years
Israel did not believe that Joseph was alive
challenge.explanation: The statement shows that knowing Joseph was alive was already a great comfort and joy to Israel.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Joseph my son” emphasize?
answers: That Joseph was Israel’s brother
Israel’s personal and fatherly relationship with Joseph
That Joseph was king over Israel
challenge.explanation: The words “my son” emphasize Joseph’s identity as Israel’s son and the emotional bond between them.

challenge.question: What additional meaning comes from the words “I will go and see him before I die”?
answers: Israel planned to send a messenger instead of going
Israel wanted to delay the meeting
Israel felt an urgency to see Joseph while he was still alive
challenge.explanation: The words show that Israel felt he needed to act promptly and meet Joseph while he was still alive.

questions.question: What can we infer from Israel’s saying, “It is enough”?
answers: The news that Joseph was alive brought Israel great joy
Israel wanted to wait several more years
Israel did not believe that Joseph was alive
questions.explanation: The statement shows that knowing Joseph was alive was already a great comfort and joy to Israel.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Joseph my son” emphasize?
answers: That Joseph was Israel’s brother
Israel’s personal and fatherly relationship with Joseph
That Joseph was king over Israel
questions.explanation: The words “my son” emphasize Joseph’s identity as Israel’s son and the emotional bond between them.

questions.question: What additional meaning comes from the words “I will go and see him before I die”?
answers: Israel planned to send a messenger instead of going

Israel felt an urgency to see Joseph while he was still alive
questions.explanation: The words show that Israel felt he needed to act promptly and meet Joseph while he was still alive.
